title: One speaker at a time, with short gaps and short overlaps

body: Conversation is not scheduled in advance. Levinson and Torreira (2015), quoting Sacks, Schegloff, and Jefferson (1974, p. 700), report the observed pattern: overwhelmingly one speaker talks at a time; more than one speaker at a time is common but brief; transitions with no gap and no overlap are common, and together with slight gaps and slight overlaps they make up the majority of transitions. The same review says a gap inside one speaker's turn is a different object from a gap between speakers, and a silence after a question is a different object again from either. This card did not re-open the 1974 article. The quotation and the distinction among pauses, gaps, silences, and lapses are taken from the 2015 review.
